walkthroughs.body_html:
Area of Study 2: Pop Music — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area of Study 2: Pop Music brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area of Study 2: Pop Music.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How does a harmonic minor scale differ from a natural minor?
options: ii to V.
The seventh degree is raised by a semitone (creating a leading note).
All notes are raised by a semitone.
It has only five notes.
Music in 3/4 time.
It has only five notes.
Three sections: A, contrasting B, and a return to A (ABA).
Three different sections (ABC).

mcqs.q: Which chords form a plagal cadence?
options: ii to V.
IV to I (the 'amen' cadence).
V to I.
It has only five notes.
